sprint_race_pace_indicator.noise_level: Low (authentic race conditions, Parc Fermé locked)

track_penalty_research.hypothesis: Circuit overtaking difficulty modulates the causal decay of starting grid penalties.

empirical_archetype_evidence.observation: Verstappen qualified P6 with championship-leading Red Bull. In race, finished P6 with 0 passes despite closing to gearbox. Penalty recovery rate: 0.0 positions per 10 laps.
empirical_archetype_evidence.conclusion: At Monaco, grid position is virtually 95% causal. Pace features cannot overcome grid rank.

empirical_archetype_evidence.observation: Verstappen started P2, passed Norris into Turn 1 on lap 1, executed superior medium-stint pace (+0.09s/lap in FP2) to win.
empirical_archetype_evidence.conclusion: Medium overtaking track enables front-row pace conversion.

empirical_archetype_evidence.case_study: Historical Spa 2022 (Verstappen won from P14) and 2023 (Verstappen won from P6)
empirical_archetype_evidence.observation: Kemmel Straight DRS enables high recovery rate (> 1.2 positions per 10 laps) for cars with > 0.5s/lap pace superiority.
empirical_archetype_evidence.conclusion: On high overtaking tracks, pace features significantly supersede grid penalty penalties.

track_penalty_research.correlation_vs_causation_summary: Grid penalty size strongly correlates with lower finishing positions on ALL circuits. However, the CAUSAL capacity of a faster car to neutralize a penalty is strictly bounded by track overtaking difficulty. Therefore, a track overtaking interaction feature is statistically and aerodynamically justified.
